brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.requirement: A shelf unit built from hex bases that holds books (open storage cells for books)
requirements.evidence: Five hex bases (half-w, full at 0,0, half-e, full at 0,-1 and 0,1) plus two 2-compartment full-depth bins in cells (0,-1) and (0,1) for books. Cell (0,0) is open with no bin. It is a cell-based storage unit, not a dedicated shelf layout, and the bins are the only book-holding parts.
Two notch drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm at cell 1,-1 and hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf at cell -1,1), each filling an empty position between touching bases. check_build reports no errors.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books (load rating)
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only; it has no load model, and the material and print choice that sets strength is up to the user. Nothing in the build establishes a 50 kg rating.

finish.summary: Built a small hex-cell shelf unit: five bases, two 2-compartment bins for books, and two notch-mounted drawers. check_build shows no errors and mesh clash is clear. The 50 kg rating cannot be verified here and is unmet; the actual strength depends on material and print settings.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
